tweets.text:
$PoUT Network (Proof of Useful Traffic) is a Rust-based blockchain research project exploring how encrypted file delivery and verifiable data traffic can replace wasteful computation as useful work. 

@PoUTNetwork dev last project went to 13million on avax chain that was dead chain, nice thread get in.

quote.text:
I've been digging into $PoUT for the last 3 days with Grok, checking the code, not just reading the posts. Here's what they've delivered.

Day by day, real commits. Their public GitHub has been updated almost daily. I cloned it and checked every update myself.

First check: 75 Rust tests passing, 23 of them brand new. Their Python reference implementation gave exactly the same results as the Rust code, and all 113 file checksums matched.

Their own review found bugs (storage accounting, validation logic), they fixed them publicly and added regression tests. Internal workspace went from 946 to 968 passing Rust tests with zero failures.

Today's commit: 52 files and over 69,000 new lines, including all 65,536 encoders (2^16) of a 4-bit test model, counterexamples, 128 deterministic request vectors and synthetic frames. I ran it: 52/52 Python tests pass, all 75 Rust tests still pass, and the checksums match for all 157 files.

Real tests, not cosmetic ones. Change a single value in the data and the tests fail immediately. Deliberately broken frames get rejected, and flipping even one bit gets caught. Everything runs offline and regenerates byte-for-byte identical, so anyone can verify it.

Honesty you rarely see. The dev openly says what's solved and what's still research, and doesn't pretend consensus is done. At this stage most devs post hype and roadmaps with zero code. Here you get commits, tests and checkable evidence, with the limitations kept visible.

A microcap with a working public repo, real tests and a dev who reports his own bugs is rare.

On top of that, there's an interesting rumor going around: the team may be connected to DegenX on Avalanche, which hit a ~$13.5M ATH back in 2023. It would explain why they're running an X account from 2022. The account has almost no reposts, but I dug into it with Grok and found that it actually reposted an Avalanche post about DegenX back in 2023. That's not hard proof, but it's a real link and it adds weight to the rumors.

DYOR, but I checked the code with Grok, and it holds up.

https://github.com/PoUTnetwork/pout-public-source-v0.1.0-2

@PoUTNetwork

tweets.text:
Over the past month I've been working on my health.

Up until this point (from 12-19 years old) I hadn't really worked out consistently.

And particularly over the past 3 years, my diet wasn't so good either.

My excuse was long hours screen-based work, standard for our industry, so I didn't have enough time.

In early September, I started waking up from my sleep with severe lower back-pain, and felt low on energy almost daily.

So I made a change.

Because I realized, buying Bitcoin constantly to acquire generational wealth over 15 years is amazing.

But if I won't be healthy enough to enjoy it... there is kinda no point.

I've been working out x4 a week for 90 days, eating clean food x3 a day, taking 5g of creatine daily, trying to get more sleep, and I feel like a new person.

Happier, sharper and more motivated.

Wealth is great, but health is equally important!

Work hard, touch grass and take care of your health :)
